column1: # Which Record Atlas region (the contract context.json, which carries the rings too) each place string this archive prints beside a date on a
# non-living person's page belongs to, for the 'at the time' notes (site/src/pages/people/[slug].astro, kit/docs/era-notes.md). One row per place
# string AS PRINTED in people.json (a Born, Baptised or Died row, and the place of a birth, christening, baptism, death, burial, residence, census,
# immigration or naturalisation event). A region of '-' means: looked at, and no Atlas region clearly covers it, so no note; the reason says why.
# A new place string in people.json fails tools/build_era.py --check until it is decided here.
# HOW THE ROWS WERE DECIDED (18 October 2026), by geometry and never by the name of a place alone: the string was reduced to its place name(s) and the
# country or province it states; the place got a point (data/era-towns.tsv: this archive's own gazetteer entries and the kit's shared cache first, then the
# GeoNames file of the Record Atlas for that country; a name that is more than one place in different rings, a bare name in several countries, and names
# in one string that are more than 120 km apart are all refused); the point was put against the RINGS of the contract. A region is named only where a
# ring contains the point and the region lists the point's country; where several rings contain it the smallest, most specific one is named
# (the others then count as neighbours in the kit's edge rule, which silences a place within 15 km of a ring edge unless the neighbour agrees).
# A region the string names itself (England, Queensland, Scotland, Ireland, Transvaal, Natal, the Orange Free State) has no point. A country, province or
# county alone (Croatia, Cape Province, a county of England), a colony (Cape Colony, Cape of Good Hope), a building or a street is '-'. A few places the
# rings reach but the region does not (Belfort, Trieste, Cabar, Jastrebarsko, Pag, Moslavina, Altona) were taken out by hand and say so.
